question.text: The risk factors section of a PPM for Yamuna Distressed Assets Fund (Category II) should include which types of risks?

answer.text: Only market risk and credit risk
Only risks that have materialized in the past for similar funds
Both fund-level risks (operational, liquidity, regulatory) and investment-level risks (sector-specific, concentration, valuation uncertainty)
Risks are not required to be disclosed as they may deter investors

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes a broad set of risks relevant to AIFs — including investor-level, fund-level, governance, liquidity, regulatory/tax, concentration, valuation and exit risks — and PPM and due-diligence material asks for strategy and risk details. A meaningful risk-factors section therefore covers both fund-level and investment-level risks. The Trap: Option A is too narrow (market and credit risk alone). Option B limits disclosure to historical events, ignoring forward-looking risks. Option D effectively suggests omitting disclosures, contradicting the disclosure framework. Note: Specific examples of risks are illustrative; the exact categorisation in any PPM follows the fund's strategy and the source-listed risk areas.
